x: Porbandar is a city and the headquarters of the Porbandar district in the Indian state of Gujarat. It is the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi and Sudama. It was the former capital of the Porbandar princely state.
xl: Porbandar and Chhaya are the twin cities, of each other and both cities are jointly governed by Porbandar–Chhaya Municipal Corporation.

x: Bhadar River is a river in the Saurashtra peninsula, in the Western Indian state of Gujarat. It flows south from its origin through Jasdan, then turns south-west and generally west until it empties into the Arabian Sea near Porbandar. The total catchment area of the basin is 7,094 square kilometres.
xl: It is impounded by two reservoirs, Bhadar-I reservoir with a capacity of 238,000,000 cubic metres, and downstream from that, Bhadar-II reservoir with a capacity of 49,000,000 cubic metres. Gondali, Chapparwadi, Phopal, Utawadi, Moj and Venu are right bank tributaries and Vasavadi, Surwa and Galolio are left bank tributaries of the river.

x: The Dhank Caves are located near Dhank village near Upleta, Rajkot district, Gujarat, India. They were chiseled out of a calcareous sandstone outcropping during the regime of the Western Satraps. The caves are influenced by Buddhist and Jain cultures.
xl: The Jain cave includes figures of Adinath, Shantinath and Pārśva. These are considered to be the earliest Jain sculptures in Kathiawad.

d: 12th century Sun temple in Gujarat, India
x: Navlakha Temple at Ghumli, Gujarat, India, is a 12th Century Sun temple built by Jethwa dynasty rulers.

d: Hindu temple dedicated to Radha Krishna in Junagadh, Gujarat
x: Shri Radha Damodar Temple is a Hindu temple, situated in the Junagadh district of Gujarat, India. The temple is dedicated to the Damodar Hari, another name of Hindu god Krishna. Within the premises of temple, Damodar kund and Revati kund are also present.
xl: In this temple, Damodar is worshiped in his four arms form of Vishnu along with his consort, goddess Radha who is seated next to him in the central shrine. This temple comes under the special care of the Government of Gujarat. Shri Damodar Pilgrimage which includes Shri Radha Damodar temple and its popular lakes - Damodar Kund and Revti Kund, is situated along the road to Girnar mountains. The renovation of this pilgrimage was done in the year 462 CE during the regime of king Skand Gupta who belongs to Gupta Empire.

x: Barda Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Gujarat, India. It is situated approximately 31 kilometres from Ranavav, 49 kilometres from Porbandar and 100 kilometres west of Gir Forest National Park. Approximately 4,00,000 people live in Barda.
xl: Previous to its 1979 establishment as a wildlife sanctuary, Barda was a private reserve for Porbandar and Jamnagar.

x: Porbandar Bird Sanctuary is a bird sanctuary in the Porbandar District of Gujarat state, India, which was dedicated in 1988. It is the only bird sanctuary in Gujarat that provides legal protection to the birds which nest there. It is small, only covering 9.33 hectares.
xl: The sanctuary has a lake attracting migratory birds and other birds such as teals, fowls, flamingos, ibis and curlews.

x: Porbandar Airport is a domestic airport and an Indian Navy base serving the city of Porbandar in the state of Gujarat, India. The airport had direct flights to Ahmedabad, Delhi and Mumbai since the 1980s, all of which were discontinued in 2020. A new terminal building was opened in April 2008.
xl: After a brief period of inactivity, the airport restarted operations in March 2025 with daily direct flights to Mumbai operated by SpiceJet, which was operated before until 2019 and 2021. Apart from civilian operations, it has a military presence in the form of INAS 343 of the Indian Navy and CGAE Porbandar of the Indian Coast Guard.

x: The Jami Masjid is a former Friday mosque, now in partial ruins, located in Mangrol, in the state of Gujarat, India. It was built in c. 1384, during the reign of the Gujarat Sultanate. The mosque is a Monument of National Importance.
xl: There are nine mihrabs in the back wall of the mosque, and the mosque structure includes an extensive subterranean vav.

d: Domestic airport in Keshod, Gujarat, India
x: Keshod Airport is a domestic airport serving the cities of Junagadh, Keshod and Veraval in the state of Gujarat, India. Spread over an area of 450 acres, it is located at Keshod, 39 km south-west of Junagadh, 4 km north-east of Keshod and 50 km north of Veraval.
